# Scientific closure requirements

These requirements govern every numbered retained-research stage. They are user requirements, not optional recommendations.

- Start from the exact verified integrated parent. Record both workflow SHA and checked-out scientific SHA.
- Commit prospective preregistration before new scientific execution. Disclose all already-known exploratory findings; never relabel them preregistered after the fact.
- Freeze mathematical objects, primary objectives, diagnostic objectives, full enumeration domain, competing outcomes, resource rules and stopping rules.
- Use algorithmically independent production and verification. Reconstruct the entire canonical universe and require exact identity equality, not supplied-record validation or count checks alone.
- Include substantive rejecting controls: missing, duplicated and substituted records; wrong values; invalid states/moves; false provenance/coverage. Preserve genuine RED evidence and failed runs.
- Provide typed mathematical arguments and distinguish general proofs, bounded evidence and unresolved propositions. No finite no-counterexample result is a universal theorem.
- Run the complete inherited foundational stack with pinned dependencies on GitHub. Inspect exact logs.
- Upload source, complete scientific certificates, logs, metadata and checksums as execution artifacts. Freshly reproduce deterministic scientific bytes in the publication job.
- Commit durable scientific evidence and verified manifests to GitHub; inspect downloaded artifact digests, not just upload success.
- Mark PR ready only after review, scientific verification and publication closure. Merge the verified head and audit the actual merge SHA, including replay, manifests, coverage and inherited stack.
- Never use CLOSED/CERTIFIED for a stage before the post-merge audit passes. Report every missing requirement explicitly.
- For barriers, primary B1, Binf and Bs are three INDEPENDENT scalar minima. LEX_BARRIER is a separate diagnostic. Their bounds need not be jointly attained by one path.
- Time is pruning / ordered recoverability update. Combinatorial barriers do not imply physical energy, action, metric, gravity or fundamental time.

Future agents must continue the complete closure chain within the user's authorized scope; recording a plan or contract does not resolve a requested run.

# Native admissibility — four-child boundary

Documented before implementation or numerical execution. Analytical proof leads developed while framing this document are disclosed in SCOPE.md; this is not a claim that those leads were prospectively preregistered.

## Carrier and extension
Use the nonempty nested-support category of the accepted v16.52 interface. The new boundary is one ordered parent with FOUR children. Each child initially supplies the accepted interface on an arbitrary finite binary/ternary tree. A proof that joining returns the identical interface would support structural induction with arities 2,3,4; that consequence must be justified, not assumed.

For a finite nonempty ordered palette P, S_root=P. Every vertex has a nonempty support S_v subset P and every child support is contained in its parent. There are no weights, new labels outside P, extra native vertices, simultaneous moves, or physical interpretation.

At internal v, h_v is the minimum size of a label set intersecting every immediate child support. Candidate target q_v is an integer 1 through arity(v). A target profile and palette are EXACTLY ADMISSIBLE only if such a nested state with h_v=q_v exists. Membership in that integer range alone does not establish feasibility on a given palette. Infeasible palettes are excluded by a proved feasibility condition, never by filtering failed constructions.

A legal primitive adds or deletes ONE label incidence at ONE nonroot vertex, preserving nonemptiness, nesting and the fixed global root. Exactness is an endpoint condition; intermediate states remain natively admitted and need not have h=q.

The claimed path budget is sum over ALL internal vertices of |h_v-q_v| <=1 at every primitive. Leaf coordinates contribute zero. Root-support changes at an attached child are legal incidences, and their effect on the four-child parent must be checked. Child normalization can spend its unit only while the parent and all other subtrees are exact.

The independent scalar barriers B1, Binf and Bs keep their inherited meanings; no lexicographic surrogate replaces them. No fundamental time, dynamics, energy, metric, gravity, or dark-matter primitive is introduced.

## Feasibility language, without an assumed width formula
Let a_i be the proved minimum palette width for child i. The compact four-root feasibility question is whether four subsets A_i of a k-label palette, with |A_i|=a_i, have transversal number q. Its equivalence to native nested-state feasibility requires proof.

Use all 15 nonempty incidence regions C subset {1,2,3,4}, with integer multiplicity n_C>=0; root-only labels may occupy the empty region. Then |A_i|=sum over C containing i of n_C. The transversal number is the least number of available region types whose union is all four indices. Repeated labels of the same region type cannot improve a minimum cover. Region multiplicities determine capacity; region support determines the cover number. No ternary width recurrence is extrapolated.

## Decisive obligations
Return the SAME six interface clauses: exact palette feasibility; compact ordered canonical endpoint; finite fixed-root normalization with total excursion <=1; exact-interior role replacement; attached compact contraction; simultaneous label/order equivariance.

Separate:
1. failure of the old proof or a chosen construction;
2. a genuine impossibility of the specified interface;
3. a nonunit barrier, requiring admitted exact endpoints and a lower bound excluding EVERY unit path.

A finite search failure, timeout, or unsuccessful normalization does not establish 2 or 3.

# Native information boundary: positive extension evidence and the action/access gap

Date: 2026-10-12. Exact inspected parent: `1dbf2e165a0b543214e6e6597fd8cca3bce46450`; tree `6a92b87a743664a0fdd98897082c3d6ed2b1027c`.

## 1. Approved question and result type

The user approved: "Given only information already justified as available to a native event, what action—if any—follows, and what retained distinction can actually be accessed?"

We first audited what the inspected implementations actually receive, then studied the information boundary exposed by the preceding view-local theorem. The audit finds conditional record/address/update interfaces, but no inspected derivation of an event-accessible complete view together with current common-carrier evidence and an action/access coupling. This is a bounded source assessment, not proof that no native event or mechanism exists anywhere in the framework.

There is a mathematical advance: full common-carrier knowledge is stronger than necessary for some safe independent pruning. Given a complete individual view, positive evidence of retained extensions has an exact, weaker safety classification. That classification is proved below. The extra evidence is not silently declared physically available. Its least-retained member is not adopted as an event law.

All deductions and controls in this note are analytic and known before review or any future numerical campaign. The old no-carrier identity theorem, the old full-carrier classification and the observation-fiber issue are not counted as new discoveries.

## 2. What the inspected sources actually justify

The eighteen exact files are bound in `native_information_boundary/source_readbacks.json`. Relative paths below are under `ResearchHistory/UQCF-GEM/`. A field present in a mathematical state or a verifier is not automatically accessible to an event or observer.

Nondeterministic interaction is eligible if its action and accessible output are derived.

The prior native-record dependency ledger and candidate C1/C3 inspections already locate many of these supplied interfaces. Rechecking them is provenance and scope work, not another obstruction theorem. The rejected native-selection argument also matters: existing order, addresses and references must not be dropped to create an artificial symmetry obstruction.

## 3. Exact question with positive current-carrier evidence

Use finite rooted prefix trees with the same concrete address convention and root o. All supplied order, Genesis and index identities are retained. Fix an indexed palette P with at least two members. A possible current common carrier T is covered by root-containing prefix-closed views (Y_i).

Let K be a fixed finite root-containing prefix-closed set of addresses certified to lie in that SAME CURRENT T. This is positive membership evidence: K is a subset of T, but it need not equal T or describe all its leaves. It may be obtained mathematically by prefix-closing a finite collection of such witnesses. That construction does not supply the certificates or their accessibility.

A deterministic rule F_i^K takes the COMPLETE own view Y, plus K and fixed index/palette data, and returns a root-containing prefix-closed subset of Y. It cannot read other views or an additional description of T. Its input may include an absence fact such as a node being terminal in Y because the complete Y is part of the contract. We do not claim positive address evidence alone supplies that absence information.

Require universal carrier preservation for every finite T containing K and every indexed cover of that T:

    union_i F_i^K(Y_i) = T.

There is no fixed hitting-profile, protected-band, source-family, extra witness-ownership or event-history promise in this quantifier. Finite T=K union Y is an allowed completion. Stronger justified promises would define a different class.

For each input Y form the finite prefix tree Q=K union Y and define

    B_K(Y) = {o} union Anc_Q(Y intersect L(Q)),

where L(Q) denotes its leaves and Anc includes the vertex itself. All these ancestors belong to Y. Equivalently, retain the ancestors of precisely those local leaves of Y that have NO strict descendant in K, together with o.

## 4. Universal safety classification

**Theorem.** The family (F_i^K) preserves the common carrier for every completion and cover specified above if and only if

    B_K(Y) subseteq F_i^K(Y) subseteq Y

for every i and every root-containing finite prefix-closed Y. The right inclusion and output type are assumptions of the class.

**Necessity.** Fix i,Y, put Q=K union Y, and choose a nonroot leaf l of Q belonging to Y. Take the possible carrier T=Q and every other input view equal to Q minus {l}. This is a valid indexed cover; removing a global leaf preserves prefix closure. K subseteq T holds even if l belongs to K. Only view i can retain l after contraction. Since i's rule has the same input (K,Y), universal carrier preservation forces l in its output. Prefix closure forces all its ancestors. The root is mandatory. Root-only cases follow directly. Thus B_K(Y) is necessary.

**Sufficiency.** Fix any actual T containing K and any cover. A global leaf l of T belongs to some Y_i. Because K union Y_i is a subset of T containing l, l is also a leaf of K union Y_i. Thus B_K(Y_i) retains l and its ancestors. Every vertex of a finite T lies above a global leaf, so the outputs cover T. QED.

This proves that B_K is the unique least retained output in the stated information class. The proof determines which contractions are universally safe; it does not determine which actual event occurs.

**Nondeterministic scope.** The same bounds hold if each local input has a nonempty set of possible output subviews and preservation is required for EVERY Cartesian combination of their choices: each possible output must contain B_K(Y). Necessity chooses any violating output and arbitrary outputs for other indices; sufficiency applies to every choice. This covers demonic independent choices, not a claimed probability law. Correlated joint outcomes, extra completion promises and interactions using other views fall outside this product contract. No theorem here forbids those architectures or demands deterministic physics.

**Information limits.** K={o} gives B_K(Y)=Y, recovering the preceding no-carrier identity result. If the complete T is provided as K, then on Y subseteq T this is H_T(Y), recovering the preceding full-carrier classification. For K_1 subseteq K_2, B_{K_2}(Y) subseteq B_{K_1}(Y): additional positive extension witnesses can only remove potentially terminal local leaves from the mandatory set. This is information ordering, not physical duration.

**Repeated action and nonselection.** B_K is idempotent. Every nonroot leaf of B_K(Y) was a retained leaf of K union Y and has no descendant in K; it remains mandatory at the second application. Prefix closure then retains the whole first output. Identity also satisfies the safety classification. Hence even with K supplied, safety does not select B_K or require nontrivial pruning.

## 5. The exact atomic certificate

Let v be a nonroot leaf of the complete own view Y. Then deleting only v is guaranteed to preserve union over all completions consistent with K,Y if and only if K contains a STRICT descendant d of v.

If such d exists, d is not in Y because v is a leaf there. Some other view covers d, and its prefix closure covers v. Thus removing v from this view cannot remove v from the union. For simultaneous independent updates, the theorem's full output bounds supply the collective guarantee; an atomic argument about an unmodified other view alone is not a scheduler.

Conversely, if K has no strict descendant of v, v is a leaf of K union Y. The adversarial completion in the theorem makes it exclusive to this view, so deleting it loses the carrier. K containing v itself is insufficient. This is a necessary-and-sufficient certificate within the declared positive-evidence information class, not a certificate-generation algorithm or a physical deletion command.

The witness need not identify which other view carries d. Coverage and prefix closure supply its existence. However, its address must refer to the same current carrier and address system; an unrelated or historical address cannot play that role.

This extension identifies a weaker requirement than full global-leaf knowledge. The preceding result did not prove full carrier access necessary; this note provides the exact intermediate case. No archive-wide originality or priority claim is made for these elementary arguments.

## 6. Rejecting controls and remaining constraints

**Mere ancestor membership.** Let Y={o,v}. With K={o,v}, completion T=Y and every other view {o} forces v to survive. Knowing v exists does not certify its redundancy.

**One positive extension.** With the same Y and K={o,v,d}, where d is a child of v, B_K(Y)={o}. This is a proof witness for permissible deletion, not a prepared physical interaction or an observer gaining knowledge. The input includes d in the current union and its absence from Y.

**One uncovered local tip blocks a larger deletion.** If Y has two terminal descendants x,y below v and K extends only x, then y remains a leaf of K union Y. Its ancestor v is mandatory even though the x branch may become removable. Evidence for one terminal branch cannot justify deleting an entire cone containing another unprotected tip.

**Stale or foreign witness.** Reusing the extension address d after the actual carrier has become T'={o,v}, or taking d from another Genesis/address system, violates K subseteq T. With Y={o,v} and other views {o}, deleting v loses the carrier. No certificate-validity conclusion follows merely from the record still storing d. If independently justified same-union evolution is maintained, membership of K persists in the union; changing the carrier requires renewed justification.

**Hitting-band safety is separate.** Set K=T in the ternary counterexample of the preceding view-local result. B_K=H_T there, and the root hitting number rises from 1 to 3. Thus partial-information classification does not produce a universal unit-band guarantee or enforce C3 floors. Single-incidence deletion has the inherited atomic bound where its same-union premises hold; repeated updates need the separate endpoint/path constraints already stated in the prior results. We insert no full-state band checker into F_i^K.

**Choice remains open.** B_K and identity can differ on the positive-extension input while both preserve union. Permitting the smaller output is not an event forcing it, nor does a nonempty set of outputs define physical probabilities or retained accessibility.

## 7. What the latest record example actually transfers

The prior five-vertex example has common root o, child u with leaves r,w, and another leaf C. In source zero, Y_a={o,u,r}; in source one, Y_a={o,u}. The memory support at u is initially identical, but the COMPLETE input view to the a-rule is already different. Under the same H_T operation, the output record R=1[a absent at u] equals 1[r absent from the initial Y_a] on those two preparations.

Therefore the operation moves a distinction already present in its full input into the declared memory coordinate. It does not acquire a previously absent distinction for an observer already given that complete input. A receiver restricted initially to the memory coordinate could gain a distinction through a derived coupling—but that receiver access and physical coupling remain precisely the missing obligations. Dependence on a system-side input is not prohibited merely because the receiver lacks it.

This is input accounting for the existing example, not a new observation-fiber impossibility theorem and not a rejection of deterministic information transfer. No claim is made that the two preparations are indistinguishable on their complete system inputs. A fixed stochastic kernel with identical complete channel inputs cannot produce source-dependent output laws merely by naming its outcomes; a native interaction with the source would change that input/action premise and must be justified separately. We do not introduce such a law here.

## 8. Answer to the approved native-event question

The source-address modules justify intrinsic prefix comparison conditional on a properly bound full address. They do not supply the needed assertion that an address belongs to the present common carrier, a complete current own view (or equivalent terminal certificate), access to those facts by the relevant event, or an actual action-to-accessible-record coupling. The adaptive event modules do contain explicit computations on already realized bits, but their event instruments/read wiring remain declared inputs. Identifying one of those bits or instruments with current view membership would insert an unearned connection.

Thus no new native action or physically accessible distinction follows from this inspected packet. The new theorem narrows what a potentially useful input could certify: a current same-carrier strict descendant plus a truthful local-terminal fact can justify the safety of a particular deletion without a global map. It does not establish that such inputs are available or that safety causes execution.

For the positive-extension independent-view route, the next eligible continuation is to identify an inherited construction that gives BOTH (i) current same-carrier membership of a strict descendant and (ii) the complete own-view/local-terminal fact to an event with a justified update relation. If that route is found, specify how a distinct receiver retains and accesses its output. A historical hash, supplied tuple, arbitrary event-bit encoding, legal-move enumerator or another successful prepared record is not that construction. It remains permissible that a derived joint or correlated architecture falls outside the independent-view class.

Reviewed disposition: **POSITIVE_EXTENSION_SAFETY_CLASSIFIED; NATIVE_INPUT_ACTION_ACCESS_UNRESOLVED**. This is a conditional information-boundary theorem and bounded input audit. Native origin/access, physical source correspondence and broad C3/C4–C6 remain OPEN. No numerical enumeration, GitHub Actions execution, historical 527-test replay, Gemini/external review, main merge or numbered-stage CLOSED/CERTIFIED claim is made. Any future numerical campaign must be prospectively frozen under AGENTS.md; these already-known deductions cannot be relabelled as unknown preregistered findings. # First-response separation under view-local carrier safety

Date: 2026-10-12 America/Phoenix / 2026-10-13 UTC.
Immutable source parent: `c96ff8b9ae0d3b3c07d4e56b51c28e4f256f3f5a`.

**Conditional analytical result. Native input availability, action and receiver access remain OPEN.** This note constructs a mathematical witness family and proves its entire permitted-output claim. It does not construct or discover a physical law. Independent argument review and publication evidence are preserved separately.

## 1. Question and advance over saturation

The preceding saturation theorem fixes the total deficit of every unextendible pruning path in a declared interval. It does not require a unique endpoint, but it still conditions its conclusion on reaching a sink. Its source pair permits an initial zero-response deletion in source one.

Can a source difference constrain the **first proper response**, without selecting a deletion location, requiring all commands to be available, or requiring completed pruning?

The answer is yes in the explicitly conditional information class below. For every integer m>=2 there are two preparations with:

- the same literal tree, ordered palette, partial current-carrier evidence K, initial internal supports and local hitting profile;
- a difference only in global-leaf incidences of the SAME indexed view a;
- a retained internal-profile bit R that is zero initially in both preparations;
- R=0 after every proper output of source zero, and R=1 after every proper output of source one, whenever the output satisfies the inherited universal independent-view safety bounds.

For a single native incidence deletion, the total deficit is exactly zero versus one. The unit-band inequality follows for that first step from the inherited atomic increment bound; a runtime full-state band filter is not needed to prove that inequality. For larger proper contractions the bit still separates the sources, but the unit band need not hold.

On this family the same bit also has a decoder using just the retained a-view at the known children of p in K. It does not require a full joint hitting-profile read. This is a mathematical reduction of the readout input, not a derivation that an event or receiver has access to that input.

This removes completion, a chosen site and maximal availability of commands from this conditional response. It does **not** derive the input certificates, event access, the physical applicability of the information/safety contract, occurrence of a proper action, or receiver access to R. An actually carrier-preserving deletion outside this information contract can fail the source separation. The explicit control below is essential.

## 2. Exact inherited information and safety contract

Use the native finite rooted-tree support representation: root support P, nonempty supports at every vertex, and child supports contained in parent supports. A label i defines a complete prefix-closed view Y_i; their union is the carrier T. The palette has at least two indices. Existing order and address identities are retained.

The positive-extension theorem supplies the following conditional class. An indexed rule has the COMPLETE own view Y_i and a common finite prefix-closed set K certified to belong to the same CURRENT carrier. It has no other view memberships or additional carrier description. It contracts its view, and carrier preservation must hold for every compatible finite carrier and cover. In the nondeterministic product version it must hold for every Cartesian combination of permitted local outputs. No source-family, fixed-profile or witness-ownership promise is inserted into that universal quantifier.

For Q=K union Y define

\[
B_K(Y)=\{o\}\cup\operatorname{Anc}_Q\bigl(Y\cap L(Q)\bigr).
\]

The inherited necessary-and-sufficient safety bound is

\[
B_K(Y_i)\subseteq Z_i\subseteq Y_i.
\]

Equivalently, a nonroot own-view leaf v can be deleted atomically with universal safety from this input if and only if K contains a strict descendant of v. A positive fact that v itself exists is insufficient. These are inherited results, not new theorems of this note.

We prove the response for EVERY joint output satisfying these bounds. Once the bounds hold, the proof does not care how the allowed outputs were chosen or correlated. We do not assert that the bounds are necessary for correlated or cross-view architectures outside the inherited information class. Nor do we assert that this class describes an already derived physical event.

A **proper output** changes at least one indexed incidence. Identity is allowed by safety and is kept separate. The one-incidence specialization uses the existing native primitive, not a newly introduced simultaneous-update rule. No scheduler, priority, largest-deletion instruction, probability distribution or guaranteed proper outcome is adopted.

## 3. One indexed source difference, with identical internal records

Fix m>=2 and an ordered palette

\[
P=\{a,c,b_1,\ldots,b_m\}.
\]

Arbitrary m here uses the inherited finite-tree definitions and the proof below. It does not extend a certified bounded-arity normalization or connectivity campaign.

The root o has children p and v. Vertex p has children u_1,...,u_m. Every u_j has two global leaves r_j,w_j; vertex v has two global leaves r_v,w_v. All addresses and the distinguished position u_1 are part of the common declared tree/reference, identical in both preparations.

Both preparations have these internal supports:

| Vertex | Common support |
| --- | --- |
| o | P |
| p | P |
| v | {a,c} |
| u_1 | {a,b_1,c} |
| u_j, j>=2 | {a,b_j} |

Only the global-leaf incidences of label a differ:

| Each indicated leaf | Source zero | Source one |
| --- | --- | --- |
| r_1,w_1 | {a,b_1,c} | {b_1,c} |
| r_j,w_j, j>=2 | {a,b_j} | {b_j} |
| r_v,w_v | {c} | {a,c} |

The complete views of c and every b_j are identical across the preparations. The complete view of a differs, so the complete system-side inputs are not indistinguishable. All supports are nonempty and nested, and the common carrier is exactly the same T.

Take the SAME partial evidence in both preparations:

\[
K=\operatorname{Anc}_T\{r_1,\ldots,r_m,r_v\}.
\]

K contains every internal vertex and one of the two leaves below each bottom parent. It omits w_1,...,w_m,w_v and therefore is strictly smaller than T. Its assertions concern current address membership, not ownership by a label. It does not contain the source answer through an a-membership field. Its validity and availability are still premises, not generated by this construction.

At o the two child supports share c (and initially a). At p all u_j supports share a. Each bottom parent has two identical child supports. Therefore the initial exact profile q is one at every internal vertex in BOTH sources. This equality includes the entire internal support record, not merely the hitting numbers.

The declared mathematical consumer is

\[
R(F)=\mathbf 1[h_p(F)>1]
     =\mathbf 1\!\left[\bigcap_{j=1}^{m} S_{u_j}(F)=\varnothing\right].
\]

Initially R=0. This is a specified internal incidence property, not an implemented sensor or a new C3 restored-marker decoder. Access to the child supports, the hitting value or this one bit is not inferred from writing the formula.

## 4. Complete permitted-output classification and proof

Every nonroot tip of each non-a view is a global leaf of T. No address in K can strictly extend such a tip. Thus B_K(Y_i)=Y_i for i!=a: the safety bounds force all non-a views to remain unchanged. This includes c, whose retained presence supplies the common cover at o.

For source zero, view a contains every node below p, and contains v but neither of v's leaves. All its p-branch tips are global leaves and therefore mandatory. The tip v is strictly extended by r_v in K. Hence

\[
B_K(Y_a^0)=Y_a^0\setminus\{v\}.
\]

There are exactly two permitted joint outputs: identity and the deletion of a at v. The unique proper output keeps c in v and in p, so h_o stays one. Every other local child-support family is unchanged. Consequently h_p=1, R=0 and total deficit D_q=0 despite a genuine nonidentity incidence change.

For source one, view a contains the p-branch internal vertices p,u_1,...,u_m but no leaf below any u_j. Its other branch contains v,r_v,w_v. Each u_j is an own-view tip strictly extended by r_j in K, whereas r_v,w_v are global leaves. Thus

\[
B_K(Y_a^1)=\{o,v,r_v,w_v\}.
\]

Every output retains that v branch. Let J be the set of u_j from which a is removed. If J is not all of {1,...,m}, prefix closure forces a to remain at p. If J is all of that set, a at p may be retained or removed. This describes all permitted outputs. The only output with J empty is identity. In particular, a proper output necessarily removes a from at least one u_j; it cannot consist solely of removing a at p while retaining a below it.

Write k=|J|. If k<m, each of the k changed child supports of p needs its own label, and none of those labels covers an unchanged child. The unchanged children share a. Thus h_p=k+1. If k=m, the remaining child supports {b_1,c},{b_2},...,{b_m} are pairwise disjoint, so h_p=m. In both cases,

\[
h_p=\min\{k+1,m\}.
\]

The c incidence remains in both p and v even when a at p is removed, so h_o stays one. All global-leaf supports remain unchanged, and every bottom hitting number stays one. Therefore

\[
D_q=\sum_{x\text{ internal}}|h_x-q_x|
   =\min\{k,m-1\}.
\]

For every proper source-one output, k>=1 and m>=2, so h_p>=2 and R=1. This proves the separation for all permitted proper outputs. The output need not be the least retained state, maximal, terminal, unique or chosen by any particular algorithm. QED.

### Decoder using one retained view

Let U=Ch_K(p)={u_1,...,u_m}. This finite address set is available from the already supplied K and the same reference p. On this exact family and all its permitted outputs, including identity,

\[
R(F)=\mathbf 1[U\not\subseteq Z_a].
\]

For source zero, every u_j remains in Z_a even when v is deleted, giving zero. For source one, U fails to be contained in Z_a exactly when J is nonempty, which is exactly the condition h_p>1 just proved. Removing p as well when J is all does not change the conclusion. Identity gives zero in both sources.

Thus a receiver supplied with the restricted retained record Z_a intersect U and the fixed reference (a,p,K) can decode the same bit without other views, global-leaf incidence reads or a complete joint hitting-profile computation.
